messages:
sam: quick heads-up — ran the onboarding sweep for quill-8b (float->int4 path) on the multi-turn chat slice. attached a short summary below. low-cost numbers look great but we're seeing quality drift on long (>1k token) dialogues.

anya: can you paste the econ calc? curious how big the win is if we keep int4 for short chats only.

sam: sure — rough calc:
```
# assume throughput & cost from bench
cost_per_gpu_hour = $3.2
tokens_per_sec = 4500
avg_tokens_per_request = 120
requests_per_hour = (tokens_per_sec * 3600) / avg_tokens_per_request
requests_per_hour # ~135000
cost_per_1M_requests = (1e6 / requests_per_hour) * cost_per_gpu_hour # ~23.7
```
So int4 gives ~2.8x token throughput vs int8 on our 8p instance, cost per 1M requests drops ~3x.

jordan: alright that math checks out. but what does "quality drift" look like? any concrete failure modes?

sam: for single-turn prompts it's fine. for multi-turn we saw hallucination spikes on factual recall and truncation/errors when KV cache reuse gets noisy. sample: user asks about previous step and model confidently invents a timestamp. precision drops ~4-6 pts on our relevance metric on long contexts.

li: could this be a decoding or temperature mismatch after quantization? did we hold sampler params constant?

sam: yes params are identical. we also tried a mild temp bump and top-p adjust — small improvement but not closing gap.

anya: product context — GTN cares about 99th pct tail for chat continuity. if long chats break, support load spikes. Do we have a hybrid route plan?

sam: proposal: route short sessions (<300 tokens/session) to int4 by default, long/active sessions to int8. fallback to int8 on detected regression signals (semantic mismatch score below threshold).

mira: devex: add a per-conversation tag in routing so product can opt-in for cheaper mode per user cohort. also expose a toggle in GTN that pins `model_variant=quill-8b-int4` for experiments.

jordan: ops: what about memory-led OOMs with int4 KV packing? infra-bot, anything risky in deployment?

infra-bot: deploy-check: quill-8b-int4 image passed smoke; KV packing uses custom allocator, tracked issue #3421 for rare index-corruption under extreme concat patterns (repro rate ~0.02%). recommend canary at 1% traffic and enable mem-safety=on.

li: curious about hybrid economics. if 30% of sessions are long, routing saves ~50% overall cost vs int8. need a metric: cost_per_conversation for cohorts. sam can you run a short sim?

sam: will run a traffic-weighted sim on prod-like traces and post numbers. preliminary: with 70/30 short/long split, overall cost drops ~45% and quality regressions are nearly eliminated by routing.

anya: preference: ship routing + canary + product toggle. for GTN recommend: 1) enable int4 for non-critical cohorts, 2) small rollout to beta users, 3) monitor semantic-coherence metric and CS tickets.

mira: I'll add a quick runbook for support: how to detect int4-induced regressions and flip cohort back to int8.

sam: thanks — I'll upload the sample slices + microbench results to the eval dashboard (link: https://redwood.internal/evals/quill8b/int4-multiturn) and post updated econ sim when done. :thumbsup:

jordan: lgtm, sync on follow-ups in tomorrow standup.
